A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text and appendices A–F. Methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite reflow and the addition of Appendix C.6.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original Local GD experiments on synthetic data and MNIST. Appendix F reports ResNet-50 experiments comparing Local SGD and Minibatch SGD on CIFAR-10.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic-data, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 experimental results in Figures 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The proposed Two-Stage Local GD and Local Gradient Flow procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.6 introduces regularization for an auxiliary theoretical baseline, without revising the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two-point synthetic problem, binary MNIST classification, and distributed ten-class CIFAR-10 classification. No evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The experimental comparisons retain the same Local GD stepsize schedules and the same Local SGD versus Minibatch SGD comparison. The regularized baselines in Appendix C.6 are analyzed theoretically, without additional experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices E–F retain the same partitions, normalization, client counts, local-step settings, learning-rate searches, training budgets, model architecture, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The studies of local-step count, stepsize schedules, and training instability are unchanged. The CIFAR-10 comparison was already present in v1; no new empirical ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revision does not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain the same experimental curves and findings, including the benefits of larger local-step counts and instability at large settings. Table 1 is also unchanged; the added formal bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.6 defines a quadratically regularized objective and proves Corollaries 4 and 5 using existing strongly convex guarantees. This is an auxiliary extension recovering the existing baselines' dominant communication complexities; the central theorems and their guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about local-step acceleration, large stepsizes, Two-Stage Local GD, and the restricted Local Gradient Flow result. Appendix C.6 supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving vanishing curvature, warmup, heterogeneity, and non-monotonic loss remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning vanilla Local GD and the restrictive client/data assumptions for Local Gradient Flow.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F retain the same data-generation instructions, partitioning details, warmup tuning, and ResNet-50 training settings. The statement excluding momentum and gradient clipping is relocated, not newly disclosed. No resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix C.6 add a direct application of Woodworth et al. (2020b) and Koloskova et al. (2020) through regularization, supplementing v1's extensions to objectives without minimizers. The bibliography and overall novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits in related work and baseline guarantees, simplifies affiliation text, and adds Appendix C.6 with a main-text pointer. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The author block becomes three columns, several long equations are wrapped differently, and Figure 2 moves to a separate final page after its discussion. Existing plots, captions, and Table 1 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.6 makes the theoretical comparison more complete by explicitly deriving regularized baselines and showing that their dominant costs match the existing baselines. This adds useful support for the comparison, while the main guarantees, experimental evidence, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
